`is_mostly_bin` no longer raises `IndexError` on inputs of 101 to 103 bytes. I haven't run the tests, as you asked.

**Cause:** When the input is longer than 100 bytes, `is_mostly_bin` in `mitmproxy/utils/strutils.py` looks at bytes 100–103 for a UTF-8 continuation byte, so it doesn't cut a character in half. It indexed `s[cut]` without checking the length. A 101-byte input has no `s[101]`, so it crashed.

**Fix:** The check is now `cut < len(s) and (s[cut] >> 6) == 0b10`. Running off the end of the data counts as a character boundary, so the cut is `s[:cut]`, which is the whole input. Results for inputs that don't hit the index error are unchanged.

**Test:** In `test/mitmproxy/utils/test_strutils.py::test_is_mostly_bin` I added a loop over lengths 101–104. It checks all-ASCII input, all-`\xff` input, and ASCII with one trailing high byte.
